subject: Renewal planning — 8→16 GPU uplift and monthly commit reprofile
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@helix.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning — dedicated capacity uplift

Jordan,

We're coming up on our annual renewal (Dec 15). After load testing this quarter our infra team wants to move from an 8‑GPU reserved pool to 16 GPUs for production (steady state) to hit our latency and throughput targets. We're especially sensitive to token cost and predictable monthly spend; procurement will need an updated monthly commit figure and a clean path for phased activation (we'd like a two‑phase cutover over the first 30 days).

Questions to start:
- What does the monthly commit look like if we double to 16?
- Can you commit to throughput SLOs for peak windows (95th percentile latency and tokens/sec)?
- Any pricing credits if we lock for 12 months versus renewing month‑to‑month?

Looping in Ben from ProcureCorp who will handle contract questions. Can we schedule a 30‑min call early next week to review?

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering
Helix.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@helix.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — dedicated capacity uplift

Samantha —

Thanks for the note and context. Great to hear the load tests look good. High level: we can support a staged uplift 8→16 with an updated monthly commit and a defined activation window. I've attached a preliminary commercial estimate to frame the numbers (attachment: Redwood_Estimate_Helix_8to16_20261121.pdf).

Initial answers:
- Monthly commit (list price → committed discount): doubling to 16 GPUs would increase the monthly committed spend from your current $48,000/mo to $88,000/mo under a 12‑month reserved commit. Exact discount depends on the final term and payment cadence.
- Throughput SLOs: we can offer a 95th percentile latency guard and a tokens/sec throughput warranty for the reserved pool under Redwood Dedicated. I'll have Avery share the SLA matrix and expected throughput ranges by model/sequence length.
- Credits: we offer a 6–12% effective credit for a 12‑month commit versus month‑to‑month depending on start date and billing alignment.

Next steps: 1) Quick call Monday 11/23 10am PT to walk the estimate and activation timeline; 2) we update an order form (I can issue a draft) and provide the SLA matrix; 3) procurement reviews final order form and we push to DocuSign.

Are you and Ben available Mon 11/23 10am PT?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@helix.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — dedicated capacity uplift

On Mon, Nov 23, 2026 at 10:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan —
> Thanks for the note and context. Great to hear the load tests look good.

Quick technical note from infra: doubling the reserved pool is straightforward. For the two‑phase cutover we typically recommend:
1) Phase 1 (week 0): activate additional 4 GPUs (soft buffer) and enable KV prefix caching for high‑qps endpoints — this buys headroom for canary traffic.
2) Phase 2 (week 2–4): ramp remainder to reach full 16 GPU capacity and move production traffic.

Throughput / SLA: attached is a short SLA and throughput matrix tuned for the model families you run (attachment: throughput_sla_matrix.xlsx). For 16 GPUs we can guarantee: 95th percentile generation latency <= 220ms for base models at seq=512 under the committed pool, and sustained 1.8M tokens/min aggregate for the pool under normal operating conditions. If you need a stricter guard we can discuss a reserved high‑priority tier.

Operational asks for activation:
- A single change window owner from Helix for the cutover (who will coordinate DNS/traffic switch).
- A rolling verification plan (sample prompts + perf checks) that Tessa can help run with your SREs.

Happy to walk through on the call now.

—Avery
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@helix.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Lawson <ben.lawson@procurecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — dedicated capacity uplift

Jordan / Avery —

Thanks for the detail and SLA draft. Ben is on board but procurement needs two clarifications before we proceed:
1) Can you confirm the monthly commit phasing? We prefer to ramp billing over the first 3 months (60% / 80% / 100%) rather than a hard immediate commit to $88k/mo — Helix's finance prefers smoother cashflow.
2) Can you add an explicit clause for fallback capacity if the 16 GPU pool experiences resource contention during a global event? We need an operational fallback (e.g., auto‑fallback to a compatible lower‑cost model + traffic shedding policy) with an escalation path.

If you can update the order form to reflect a 3‑month billing ramp and the fallback clause, procurement can get this through legal quickly. We'll aim to sign before Dec 10.

—Samantha
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@helix.ai>, Ben Lawson <ben.lawson@procurecorp.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Final commercial summary & next steps — HLX 8→16 uplift (Order Form draft)

Samantha / Ben —

Thanks — we've updated the order form and outlined the operational fallback. Summary below (order form attached as OrderForm_HLX_8to16_20261129.pdf):

Commercial summary (12‑month term):
- Capacity: Reserved pool upgrade from 8 GPUs → 16 GPUs (Redwood Dedicated).
- Monthly committed spend: $88,000/mo effective starting Month 1. Billing ramp applied over first 3 months (billed at 60% / 80% / 100% of the committed amount; invoices reflect ramp schedule).
- One‑time activation fee: $6,000 (staged activation & ops runbook).
- Effective commit credit: 6.5% applied to list rates for the 12‑month term.
- Throughput SLO: 95th pct gen latency <= 220ms at seq=512; sustained pool throughput 1.8M tokens/min. Escalation contacts and on‑call are in the order form.
- Fallback behavior: automatic model variant downgrade + traffic shedding trigger during global resource contention; Redwood will notify and enact fallback within 2 minutes of detection. Detailed runbook attached.

Next steps:
1) Ben to confirm procurement language and sign order form via DocuSign link (included in attachment and below).
2) On receipt of signed form we target staged activation Week 1 of Jan (we'll coordinate exact dates).
3) Tessa will share the verification checklist and run the first canary tests with your SREs.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=prod&acct=12345&v=8a3f
HubSpot deal: https://app.redwood.com/deals/HLX-2026-REN-004

Please let me know if anything else is needed — otherwise we'll issue the DocuSign envelope and route to Ben for signature.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Redwood Inference
